args.command:
git add src/error.rs src/main.rs tests/post_commit_publication.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(beadrs-122de256): define split-failure semantics for post-commit publication

A mutation that commits and then fails automatic publication now reports
the split as a defined outcome instead of surfacing as a generic internal
error whose exit-1 was an accident of the catch-all arm (plan 6.2.1 item
5, ADR-003, R026 step A5).

The chokepoint's fallible tail moved into publish_committed_state, and
every failure from it -- lock acquisition included -- is wrapped in a
dedicated Error::PostCommitPublicationFailed whose message states the
split outright: the mutation is still committed and visible, exit 1 never
means it was rolled back, the durable checkpoint did not advance, and
'bead sync flush-only' publishes it (the ADR-007 name-the-remedy rule).
The variant pins exit 1 explicitly in exit_code() so the mapping cannot
drift with whatever the underlying publication error would have mapped
to. The disarm paths (no connection, unreadable sequence, nothing to
publish) remain silent successes.

The contract is observable exactly as the plan specifies: the mutation's
own success output stays alone on stdout, the failure lands on stderr,
and the process exits 1 -- so a machine consumer can distinguish "the
mutation did not happen" from "the mutation happened and the checkpoint
did not advance" by the preserved success output. The forced-failure
test now asserts the whole contract: exit exactly 1, one-line stdout,
split-naming stderr, the issue still present and listable afterward, a
genuinely dirty checkpoint, and the named remedy closing the gap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -3

content:
Done — bead `beadrs-122de256` closed and pushed.

## What shipped (commit `671d70d`)

The chokepoint already ran publication after commit, but a publication failure surfaced as a generic `Internal` error — exit 1 only by accident of the catch-all arm, with nothing telling a machine consumer the mutation had committed. The split outcome is now a defined thing:

- **`src/error.rs`** — new `Error::PostCommitPublicationFailed` carrying the underlying publication error as `source`, with an explicit `exit_code()` arm pinning 1 (so the mapping can't drift with whatever the wrapped error would have mapped to). The message names the split outright: *the mutation is still committed and visible — exit 1 here never means it was rolled back; the durable checkpoint did not advance; run `bead sync flush-only` to publish it* (the ADR-007 name-the-remedy rule).
- **`src/main.rs`** — the chokepoint's fallible tail (lock acquisition through pointer commit) moved into `publish_committed_state`; every failure from it is wrapped into the dedicated variant. The disarm paths (no connection, unreadable sequence, nothing to publish) stay silent successes — decisions not to publish, not failures to.
- **`tests/post_commit_publication.rs`** — the forced-failure test now asserts the whole contract: stdout holds exactly the new issue ID, stderr carries the split wording + remedy, exit code is exactly 1, the issue is still present and listable afterward, the checkpoint is genuinely dirty (covered < live), and the named remedy closes the gap.

Verified live in a scratch workspace: `exit=1`, stdout = `demo-01d455c8` alone, stderr = the split message. `cargo fmt` / `clippy -D warnings` clean, full suite **750 passed / 0 failed**.

## Two operational notes

- Closing the bead exposed that `~/.cargo/bin/bead` is a stale 0.1.3 build (no `sync status`, no auto-flush) — its `bead close` left the checkpoint dirty, so I flushed with the current local binary and committed the closure as `1fec3cf`. That flush also applied 38 accumulated tombstones, so the checkpoint object set shrank by ~3.5k lines. I saved a memory about the stale binary.
- The R026 default is untouched: auto-flush stays gated off, so this split outcome only arises in workspaces that opt in via `checkpoint.auto_flush`.
